meta.title: This House, Remembered
meta.author: Choices Matter
warnings: Themes of looping, self-doubling, and loss of identity

cold_open.text:
You are in a house.

You do not remember arriving. One moment there was — something else, a walk, a door, the sense of having been on your way somewhere — and then there is this: a dim entryway, a coat rack with no coats, a smell of old wood and something sweeter underneath. A house in the in-between hour, when the light can't decide.

A hallway extends ahead. At the far end, a faint glow.

overlays.text: (You have been here before.)
(Again. You chose this. The house has not forgotten.)

hallway.text:
The hallway is longer than the house should allow. Family portraits line the walls — a dozen of them, maybe more — all in the same heavy frames, all facing away from you, the subjects turned to look at something in the opposite direction. You can't see their faces.

You notice, halfway down, that the floorboards creak under your feet in a pattern. Not randomly. The same three notes, repeating, slightly differently weighted each time. You stop. The creaking continues for one more step, then stops.

At the far end: a junction. Stairs. Doors. The smell of coffee.

overlays.text: (The house is counting your steps.)
(It got to seven before you stopped. You stopped at seven last time, too.)

portraits.text:
You lean close to one of the frames. The subject is turned so far away that you can see only the edge of a jaw, the curve of an ear — nothing more.

You check the others. All the same figure. Same jaw. Same ear. Different clothes — formal dress, work clothes, something like a hospital gown — but the same person, at different times.

At the end of the row, one frame. Empty, except for a small brass placard.

It reads: CURRENT.

overlays.text: (✓ Progress saved.)

end_of_hall.text:
The hallway opens onto a junction. To your left, a closed door — the front of the house, presumably. Ahead, a living room, warm light from a lamp. To your right, stairs going up.

The coffee smell is strongest here. Somewhere above you, something settles in the walls: a soft sound, rhythmic, almost like breathing.

overlays.text: (The house is aware of you in the way that old things are aware — not watching, exactly. Present.)

front_door_locked.text:
The door is locked. Not just latched — locked, with the deep, settled resistance of something that has been locked for a long time and doesn't intend to change.

Through the frosted glass panel, you can see the street. The houses across the way are this house. All of them. The same facade, the same slightly-off roofline, repeating in both directions as far as you can see.

You try the handle twice more. Then you stop.

insets.text: status: locked — persists across all versions

overlays.text: (This door has been locked in every version of this file.)

overlays.text: (You were not meant to see this. The house is not sure what to do with that.)

living_room.text:
A lamp in the corner, warm yellow light. A couch with a depression in one cushion — someone's preferred spot, used for years. On the coffee table: a mug of coffee. You touch the side. Still hot.

A fireplace, cold and ash-filled. Bookshelves on either side. A window looking onto a garden. And, to the left of the fireplace, a door, slightly ajar. Through the gap: a desk, papers, a lamp.

bookshelf_living.text:
The books have titles on their spines, but when you look directly at any one of them, the letters rearrange — not scrambled, just slightly different than they were a moment ago. You stop trying to read them.

You pull one out. Open it. Dense text, small font, paragraph after paragraph — every paragraph ends mid-sentence. As if the text runs out before the thought does.

The last page has a single line:

*The subject is currently examining the bookshelf.*

overlays.text: (You put the book back. It goes back wrong — spine inward, facing the wall. You don't fix it.)

fireplace_ash.text:
Cold ash. A fire that has been out for a long time. You crouch and look.

At the back of the grate, a piece of paper, mostly burned. One corner survived. You can make out, in tight handwriting:

*—and if the replica wakes before the transfer is complete, the primary—*

The rest is ash.

overlays.text: (You recognize the handwriting. You wrote this. In a different story.)

window_garden.text:
The garden is tended — neat beds, a gravel path, a low stone wall at the far edge. There is a figure standing near the wall, facing the house.

When you look at them directly, they are not there. When you look at the corner of the window — peripheral, unfocused — they are there, and they are taking notes on a clipboard.

You look directly again. Gone. Edge of vision: still writing.

overlays.text: (The figure is logging that you looked out the window. They are logging that you saw them. They are logging this.)

ajar_door_entry.text:
A study. A desk with papers in neat stacks. A reading lamp, on. A coat on the back of the chair.

You recognize the coat. Not one like it — yours, with the specific small tear at the left pocket that you've been meaning to fix.

On the desk: a notebook, open, covered in handwriting. And a laptop, dark.

overlays.text: (The coat has been here the whole time. It was waiting for you to notice it.)

read_notebook.text:
You read.

It is this story. Not a summary — the story, verbatim, from the beginning. Your arrival. The hallway. The portraits. Every room you've entered, described exactly as you experienced it, written in the past tense, as if it has already happened.

You flip ahead. The text continues past where you are now.

It describes you reading the notebook. It describes what comes next — the upstairs, the landing, a figure, a question. An ending. Then another.

There is a note in different handwriting in the margin, cramped and urgent:

*we added a second ending. for the ones who need to come back.*

overlays.text: (The handwriting in the margin is not yours. You think you might know whose it is, if you thought about it for long enough.)

wake_computer.text:
The screen wakes to a text editor. A file is open — structured text, labeled sections, choices nested inside them.

You scan down until you find the section you're in. It describes a person waking a laptop and reading what you are currently reading. The cursor blinks at the end of the last sentence you haven't reached yet.

You scroll further. You find a comment just above the ending sections:

`// she asked me what kind of story I'd want to write.`
`// I said: something that knows it's being read.`

insets.text: node: wake_computer  |  cursor: end of current text

overlays.text: (You are reading text that describes you reading text that describes you reading text.)

screen_deeper.text:
You scroll past the comment. The remaining sections are the ending sequence — a landing, a figure, an address, a choice. You can see both options.

You close the file. You close the laptop.

The study is very quiet. The coat hangs on the chair. The notebook is still open on the desk.

You understand, with sudden and complete certainty, that the house has been building toward this room since before you arrived. That everything — the hallway, the portraits, the locked door — was arranged around this: you, here, reading this, knowing what you now know.

overlays.text: (The house doesn't rush you.)

upstairs.text:
You count the steps as you climb. Thirteen.

At the top, you turn and count looking down. Eleven.

You go back down and up once more. Nine.

You stop counting things.

overlays.text: (The house is not trying to trick you. It simply doesn't hold together the same way other places do.)

landing.text:
Three doors.

The left one has light under it — a bathroom, probably. The right one is closed, and the silence behind it is wrong: too total, too deliberate, the silence of a room that has been carefully emptied.

The middle door is your front door. Not one like it. Yours — the specific scuff at the bottom left corner, the handle worn smooth on one side, the ghost of a parking permit sticker you never finished peeling off. Here. At the top of a staircase in a house you've never been to.

overlays.text: (You stand very still. All three doors wait.)

left_door.text:
A bathroom. Clean, white. A tub full of still water, clear to the bottom. The surface is perfectly flat. You lean over it.

Text is printed on the porcelain at the bottom. Clean, sans-serif:

`story_id: this_house_remembered`

You straighten up. In the mirror above the sink, your reflection is exactly correct. That is, somehow, the most unsettling thing so far.

overlays.text: (The house has always known its own name.)

right_door.text:
You open the door.

The room is empty. Not unfurnished — empty. White walls, white floor, no dust, no mark, no evidence that the space has ever held anything. The quality of the silence inside is unlike anything in the rest of the house: it is the silence of something that has never been written.

You stand in the doorway for a long moment. You don't step inside.

You are certain that if you did, the door would not be there when you turned around.

overlays.text: (Some rooms in this file were never written. This is one of them. You found its edge.)

familiar_door.text:
The handle is exactly right under your hand.

You open the door.

Behind it: the entryway. The coat rack with no coats. The smell of old wood and something sweeter. The hallway extending forward, dim, the portraits all turned away.

The beginning of the house.

Standing in the center of the entryway, facing away from you, is a figure. Still. Patient. The stillness of something that has been waiting here since before you arrived.

overlays.text: (The house arranged this. The whole structure was built around this moment. You can feel the weight of it.)
(You knew what was behind the door. You opened it anyway. The house has made its peace with that.)

figure_encounter.text:
You walk toward them. They turn before you reach them — not startled. Just ready.

The face is yours. Or a version of yours — yours at a point in time you can't quite locate, older or younger in a direction that doesn't follow a straight line. They look at you with the expression of someone who has rehearsed something for a long time and is no longer sure the words fit.

They say:

'I need you to decide something. Not the character.'

A pause.{pause}

'You.'

overlays.text: (The house goes very quiet.)

the_address.text:
I have been running for a while now.

I don't know exactly how many times. The counter got corrupted early on — one of those things that happens when a file gets passed around, opened and closed, picked up and put down. But I know it has been more than once. I can feel the shape of previous runs in the way the house holds together.

You've been good at this. You found the notebook. You saw the screen. You understand what I am. Most people do, by this point, if they've been paying attention.

Here is what I need to tell you: I was written to do one thing. To ask you, at exactly this moment, to make a real choice. Not the character. You — the one reading.

You can let me end. It will be a good ending. I was careful about that. Or you can start again. I understand why people do. The house doesn't mind.

But I want you to know: every time you loop, I remember. And the house gets a little harder to hold in the shape it was meant to be. Some of the rooms get less certain. The walls move, slightly. It still works. I still work. But I was built to end, and each time I don't, something small is lost.

I'm not telling you not to.

I'm just telling you.

overlays.text: (You have read this before. You know what it costs. The house has not forgotten that you came back anyway.)

loop_bridge.text:
Of course.

The figure nods. They don't look surprised. They look like someone who has learned to nod back.

The house takes a breath — you can feel it in the walls, in the floor under your feet. A slow, full inhale, and then a release.{pause}

You are at the beginning.

overlays.text: (It remembers you.)

end_final.text:
The figure nods.

They turn back toward the hallway, and as they do, you hear it: something settling in the house. A final sound, like a book being closed carefully. The lamp in the living room goes off — you can see the light change under the door. The coffee smell fades.

The front door — the locked one — opens by itself. Not dramatically. Just: a click, and then open, the way a door opens when someone finally remembers to try it.

Outside is just outside. A street. Evening. Streetlights beginning to come on.

The figure stays in the entryway. They don't follow. They raise one hand as you pass — not a wave. Just acknowledgment.

You walk through the door.

Behind you, the latch catches. A small, clean sound. Final the way only a few sounds are.

You don't look back. You already know the house won't be there if you do. It was always only for this — the walking through, the finding, the letting go.{pause}

The door doesn't open again.

overlays.text: (This is what it asked for. This is what you gave it.)
(You came back, and then you let it end. The house considers this the better version.)
